question: A warehouse manager organized boxes. Starting: 77 boxes. He multiplied by 2 to double the inventory. He subtracted 81 for shipment. He added 26 back. He added 57 more. He added 36 final boxes. How many boxes are in the warehouse?

A retail manager tracked inventory. Starting: 30 items. She multiplied by 5 for display. She added 63 items. She subtracted 74 for sales. She subtracted 3 damaged. She multiplied by 4 for ordering. How many items are ordered?

A student tracked assignments. He started with 34 assignments. He subtracted 30 completed. He added 16 new ones. He multiplied by 4 for review sessions. He subtracted 68 from review. He added 44 bonus. Morning through evening studying. How many assignments total does he have?
A venue manager planned capacity. Starting: 40 seats. He added 61 seats. He subtracted 4 for safety. He subtracted 51 for accessibility. He subtracted 22 for staff. How many seats remain for guests?

Two managers, Helen and Rick, oversaw sales. Rick managed 117 units. He multiplied by 3 for promotion. He added 79 bonus items. He added 50 from partnerships. He multiplied by 2 for year-end projection. Helen supervised the morning team. How many units in the annual projection?

A library tracked books. Starting collection: 141 volumes. She added 12 new purchases. She divided by 3 to create sections. She added 78 donations. She added 58 more. She subtracted 48 lost items. How many books total in the collection?

A warehouse manager counted items. Morning inventory: 180 units. He added 7 more. He added 63 others. He subtracted 61 for shipment. He subtracted 50 damaged. One distractor: the previous day had 95 units. How many items remain?

A factory tracked output. Starting production: 224 items. He added 15 rush orders. He subtracted 165 for recall. He multiplied by 9 for next week's demand. He added 72 bonus items. Working through morning, afternoon, and evening. How many items projected for next week?

A venue manager planned events. Starting bookings: 46 events. He subtracted 11 cancellations. He added 44 new bookings. He added 80 additional slots. He subtracted 139 conflicts. Morning through evening scheduling. A distractor: last month had 55 events. How many available events remain?

Two consultants, Lisa and Tom, compared projects. Tom had 98 active projects. He added 77 new initiatives. He subtracted 42 completed. He added 52 proposals. He multiplied by 5 for scaling. He added 70 contingency projects. Converting to days needed at a dozen per day, how many days of work?

A performer prepared routines. Starting material: 23 minutes. She subtracted 21 for cuts. She added 78 new material. She multiplied by 9 for a multi-hour show. She divided by 5 for segment time. Converting to hours, how many minutes per segment?

A manufacturer scaled production. Starting run: 224 items. He multiplied by 2 for double shift. He multiplied by 7 for weekly demand. He multiplied by 6 for monthly supply. He added 56 bonus items. He worked morning through evening. How many items monthly?

Two partners, Frank and Emma, compared stores. Frank's store started with 186 items. He added 31 from a transfer. He added 22 from a donation. He added 24 more from inventory. He doubled for promotion pricing. Emma managed another location. One distractor: the warehouse had 75 items. How many items in Frank's store for promotion?

Two rivals, Susan and Maria, compared sales. Susan started with 61 items. She multiplied by 9 for aggressive marketing. She subtracted 321 returns. She multiplied by 6 for next campaign. She multiplied by 7 for year-end push. Maria had similar metrics. How many items projected for year-end?

A producer organized content. Starting collection: 134 items. He added 29 pieces. He added 72 more. He multiplied by 3 for distribution channels. He subtracted 83 for licensing issues. How many items distributed?

Three colleagues tracked a complex project. Beginning stage: 175 tasks. She multiplied by 3 for planning. She divided by 3 (cancelling to 175). She multiplied by 4 for execution. She subtracted 516 completed. She added 77 new tasks. She added 17 contingency. How many tasks remain?

A business scaled rapidly. Starting capacity: 99 units. He subtracted 97 for maintenance. He added 68 new equipment. He multiplied by 8 for efficiency gains. He multiplied by 9 for scale. He multiplied by 8 for redundancy. Converting to labor hours, how many hours of production?

A student analyzed results. Starting data: 29 points. She added 77 observations. She multiplied by 6 for analysis weight. She divided by 4 for normalization. She subtracted 27 for exclusions. One distractor: she had 40 backup observations. How many weighted points remain?

Two architects, Nicole and David, budgeted a renovation. Starting estimate: 184 dollars in thousands. She added 23 more. She multiplied by 5 for materials. She added 74 for labor. She subtracted 811 for efficiency gains. She subtracted 188 for volunteer work. Converting to thousands, how much is the final budget?

A publisher tracked manuscripts. Starting pile: 213 pages. She multiplied by 5 for editing passes. She multiplied by 8 for printing. She added 24 illustrations. She added 79 bonus pages. She multiplied by 7 for distribution units. Morning through evening production. How many units for distribution?

Two teammates, Alex and Jordan, managed project loads. Alex began with 87 tasks. He added 33 new ones. He multiplied by 5 for complexity weighting. He multiplied by 4 for team members. He divided by 6 for even splitting. He divided by 2 for simplification. How many tasks per person?

A student studied for exams. Starting hours: 26 of study time. She divided by 2 for concentration. She added 52 from group sessions. She added 20 from tutoring. She multiplied by 2 for review cycles. She added 68 final cramming hours. A distractor: her friend studied a dozen hours. How many total study hours?

A gardener cultivated beds. Starting plots: 35. He added 26 spring plantings. He added 57 summer crops. He multiplied by 7 for variety. He added 63 bonus plants. He subtracted 850 for space constraints. Converting to hours to plant at a dozen per hour, how many hours needed?

A collector expanded inventory. Starting collection: 151 items. Added 57 new acquisitions. Added 71 from a donation. Added 78 from an auction. Added 23 bonus pieces. Multiplied by 6 for cataloging. A dozen reference items were mentioned. How many total items cataloged?

A researcher compiled data. Starting sample: 94 readings. Added 4 calibration points. Subtracted 21 for outliers. Subtracted 50 for errors. Multiplied by 2 for verification. Multiplied by 7 for final analysis. How many verified data points?
